subject: MSA: venue, governing law, and emergency relief protocol
messages:
From: Andrew Smith <andrew.smith@harrowtech.com>
To: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: HarrowTech Legal <legal@harrowtech.com>, Lily Chen <lily.chen@harrowtech.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HarrowTech - MSA: governing law and injunctive relief

Naomi,

Thanks for the draft MSA — our legal team flagged the governing law and emergency relief language as potential blockers for procurement. Two items in particular:

1) Governing law: Harrow prefers New York (to align with our standard contracts) but we are open to discussing a compromise.

2) Injunctive/equitable relief: we need to ensure that Harrow can bring timely injunctive relief in our chosen courts when necessary (data protection incidents or IP misuse). Your current arbitration-forward approach may delay emergency access.

I've attached a short list of our concerns (HT_GovLaw_Questions.pdf). Can you propose a narrow carve that preserves your arbitration preference but allows immediate injunctive relief in court for the most urgent categories?

If possible, please provide suggested clause language by EOD tomorrow — procurement needs to sign off before we can proceed to SOW.

Best,
Andrew
Andrew Smith
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
HarrowTech

From: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Smith <andrew.smith@harrowtech.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HarrowTech - MSA: governing law and injunctive relief

Andrew — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. We absolutely want to avoid a hard stop on procurement. High-level: Redwood remains committed to arbitration for the bulk of disputes (we've found it reduces cost and time for both parties), but we are willing to accept a narrow, limited carve for emergency equitable relief where immediate court intervention is necessary.

Proposed compromise (draft language attached as RNW_GovLaw_Proposal.docx):
- Governing law: Company law of the State of California (substantive law only) for interpretation of the Agreement.
- Dispute resolution: Binding arbitration (AAA rules) for all disputes except as follows.
- Emergency equitable relief carve: Either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in the state or federal courts located in the Northern District of California (this remedy is limited to claims seeking to prevent imminent data exfiltration, unauthorized access to confidential data, or clear misappropriation of Redwood's intellectual property). All other claims proceed to arbitration.
- Emergency relief protocol: Parties agree to an expedited notice and teleconference requirement (Redwood to provide initial written notice, then a 48-hour expedited teleconference to seek to narrow issues before any emergency filing, unless irreparable harm is imminent).

Rationale: this preserves arbitration for commercial disputes while ensuring Harrow can act quickly in a true emergency. If you cannot accept CA as the governing law, we can discuss a neutral compromise (e.g., Delaware) but would like to keep the emergency relief court seat in the Northern District of California.

Two asks: (1) can your team confirm whether the carve scope above (data exfil/IP/unauthorized access) is narrow enough for procurement? (2) If not, propose the exact categories you need preserved tomorrow so we can iterate quickly.

Thanks — copying Soojin and Marissa for legal redline support.

—
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Operations (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RNW_GovLaw_Proposal.docx

From: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: HarrowTech MSA - venue carve proposal and escalation playbook

Marissa/Soojin — quick internal note following Andrew's ask and my reply. Procurement wants to keep their court access; Harrow's preference is NY but they sign off if they can get timely injunctive relief. My external proposal (attached RNW_GovLaw_Proposal.docx) should get us 80% of the way there. I have two suggested refinements from a risk/ops perspective:

1) Broaden emergency categories slightly to include (a) subpoenas/third-party preservation directed at Redwood-hosted data when Harrow has a lawful request, and (b) direct risks to customer production environments (not just data exfiltration). Keep language narrow and enumerated.

2) Add a short "Emergency Escalation & Notice" appendix (see Emergency_Relief_Playbook.pdf) that lays out:
   - 24-hour notification windows where feasible,
   - 48-72 hour expedited coordination call to attempt a mutual stay or other remedy, and
   - an explicit instruction that either party may proceed to court immediately if irreparable harm is imminent (and all arbitration deadlines are tolled by filing for emergency relief).

3) If Harrow pushes back on CA governing law, propose Delaware as an alternate neutral seat for arbitration while keeping the emergency court seat in the Northern District of California. This split is unusual but we've used it successfully before and it limits cross-border enforcement friction.

Can you draft a clean redline combining my external draft and these two refinements? I'd like to send by tomorrow morning to keep procurement moving.

Thanks — Naomi

Attachment: Emergency_Relief_Playbook.pdf

From: Lily Chen <lily.chen@harrowtech.com>
To: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Andrew Smith <andrew.smith@harrowtech.com>
Cc: HarrowTech Legal <legal@harrowtech.com>
Date: 2028-04-29T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HarrowTech - MSA: governing law and injunctive relief

Naomi — appreciate the fast back-and-forth and the pragmatic proposal. Procurement and Legal reviewed the redline and Harrow can accept the carve as written with one small change: please shorten the expedited coordination call window from "48-72 hours" to "48 hours" (procurement wants a consistent SLA).

We are amenable to the split approach: substantive governing law can be California, arbitration for most claims (Delaware as fallback if needed), and the Northern District of California for emergency injunctive relief limited to the enumerated categories. We've attached the executed redline (Executed_Redline_v3.docx) that incorporates the 48-hour change and a couple non-substantive cleanup edits.

If that's good on your side, we'll route for final signature and send the DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Lily Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
HarrowTech

Attachment: Executed_Redline_v3.docx
